text:
maria: Rolling BIOS 2.1.4 -> starting canary in us-west-2 GPU pools in 30m. This build toggles Secure Boot enforcement (UEFI var) and BMC microcode update. Expect OOB session reset during postflash. Pausing canary if >3% failed boots. LMK concerns.
kevin: Copy. Which racks / jumphosts? Any Reserved/Dedicated pools in canary set?
sara: Oncall: I'll watch provisioning queue. If serial-console flaps, can we auto-route inference to eu1 with model fallback? cost implications?
maria: Canary set = r-uw2-gpu-1..4 (non-dedicated). Dedicated customers excluded. We'll still hit shared 'on-demand' GPU capacity for a handful of jobs.
devops: If OOB reboots persist, we can spin warm standby capacity in us-west-2 (2x g4dn) — cost ~ $1.2k/day. Prefer to avoid unless >5% capacity loss.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: BIOS 2.1.4 canary scheduled at 2025-11-02T00:30:00Z. Rolling window 4 hours. Auto-rollback threshold=3%.
kevin: @maria if BMC update toggles secureboot, do we need to reissue attestation keys? Runbook?
maria: We set 'secureboot-flip' policy to only set enforcement flag, not update KEK/PK. No key reissue expected. Runbook: 1) if netcat OOB fails, attempt `ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U redwood -P <redacted> chassis power cycle` 2) if console unresponsive after 2 cycles, escalate to hardware ops.
sara: Canary health check queries: `curl -s http://health-proxy/usw2/canary | jq .boot_status` expecting 'ok' within 90s.
linda: note: We've seen nvram bitflip on board rev C after previous secboot flips — watch nvram scrub logs: `/var/log/oob/nvram-scrub.log`
kevin: Agree. If we see nvram errors, pause and run `oob-provisioner rollback --to-tag=2.1.3`
maria: I'll set a policy to pause automatically on nvram errors >1%. Also enabling minimal autoscale to avoid mass evictions.
sara: :thumbsup: I'll put a notification in #incidents if automated pause triggers. Oncall: @kevin @linda
kevin: I'll be near laptop. PS: we should pre-warm kernel cache on fallback nodes to reduce cold-start latency.
devops: Suggestion: instead of full warm standby, use short-term burst via partner capacity — cheaper but only in same region. Could reduce inter-region spillover.
sara: OK roadmap: monitor +30m, escalate if failures >1% for 15m, pause >3% immediate. Cost path: if spillover->eu1 > 100qps for >1hr alert FinOps.
oncall-bot: oncall-bot: paging kevin, sara — health alert rule 0 will trigger at 1759992280 if canary boot_fail_count>3
linda: Also snapshot GPU VMs pre-flash (`gcloud compute snapshots` / image-store) — in case we need to reprovision quickly.
maria: Thanks. I'll post follow-ups with exact rack IDs and command snippets. Starting pre-canary prep now.
